BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# LEGAL MEMORANDUM

**TO:** Amelia Frost & Project Kestrel Deal Team (Wattlebridge Holdings)  
**FROM:** Buyer Legal Advisory  
**DATE:** 24 September 2026  
**SUBJECT:** Project Kestrel – Detailed Legal Review and Pushback Strategy: Seller SPA Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

---

### 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

We have critically reviewed the Seller’s (Harbourglass Ventures) draft SPA updates and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003) against the **Wattlebridge Holdings Buyer Negotiation Playbook**. 

The Seller’s draft departs substantially from our required playbook positions across almost every critical legal commercial term. Notably, the Seller attempts to subject fundamental title/capacity, tax, IP, and fraud risks to a standard, narrow general liability regime (capped at 20% / 18 months), while relying on unverified internal records and shifting post-completion liabilities onto the Buyer. 

**Note on Fallback Approvals:** Under our Playbook, a 20% general warranty cap (AUD 4,800,000) and an 18-month limitation period are conditional fallbacks usable **only with your express, prior written authority identifying the specific draft**. No such approval has been granted. Therefore, we must firmly reject these positions and reinstate our baseline terms (25% cap / 24 months).

Below is our comprehensive analysis of the material departures, followed by concrete negotiation recommendations.

---

### 2. DETAILED DEPARTURES & LEGAL ANALYSIS

#### A. Liability Caps, Thresholds & Time Limits (Clauses 12.1, 12.2, 12.3, 13)
* **General Warranty Cap (Clause 12.1):** The Seller proposes a cap of 20% of the Purchase Price (AUD 4,800,000). 
  * *Playbook Position:* Baseline is 25% (AUD 6,000,000). The 20% cap is a fallback requiring written authorization from Amelia Frost.
  * *Analysis & Action:* In the absence of written authorization, we must reject the 20% cap and insist on 25% (AUD 6,000,000).
* **De Minimis & Basket (Clause 12.2):** The Seller proposes a de minimis of AUD 25,000, a basket of AUD 250,000, and specifies that only the *excess* above the basket is recoverable (deductible basket).
  * *Playbook Position:* De minimis of AUD 5,000; aggregate basket of AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the *first dollar* once exceeded (tipping basket).
  * *Analysis & Action:* The Seller’s proposed thresholds severely impair our ability to recover legitimately aggregated losses. We must reject the AUD 25k de minimis, AUD 250k basket, and deductible structure. Revert to AUD 5k de minimis and AUD 50k first-dollar tipping basket.
* **General Limitation Period (Clauses 12.3 / 13):** The Seller limits general warranty claims to 18 months post-Completion.
  * *Playbook Position:* 24 months post-Completion. 18 months requires written authorization from Amelia Frost.
  * *Analysis & Action:* Reject 18 months; reinstate the 24-month general claims window.

#### B. Fundamental / Title Warranties, Tax, and IP Regimes
* **Fundamental & Title Claims:** The Seller proposes that title and capacity warranties be subject to general warranty caps, baskets, and time limits for "administrative simplicity."
  * *Playbook Position:* Title and fundamental warranties must be governed by a separate regime: 100% Purchase Price cap (AUD 24,000,000), at least 6 years (72 months) limitation period, and excluded from de minimis, baskets, and knowledge bars.
  * *Analysis & Action:* Subjecting ownership of the target shares to a 20%/18-month cap is unacceptable. We must carve out Fundamental and Title claims into a separate regime with a 100% cap and a minimum 6-year period.
* **Tax & IP Warranties:** The Seller asserts that Tax and IP warranties are settled under the general regime.
  * *Playbook Position:* Tax and IP terms remain OPEN. Categories must remain separate with tailored protections.
  * *Analysis & Action:* Reject the Seller's blanket subsumption of Tax and IP. Require a dedicated Tax Indemnity/Warranties regime (typically matching statutory limitation periods, e.g., 6–7 years) and separate IP indemnity protections.

#### C. Carve-Outs for Fraud and Misconduct (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)
* **Seller Position:** The Seller applies limitation caps, exclusive remedies, and non-reliance clauses to *all* claims of any nature without exception.
* **Playbook Position:** Fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all liability caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy provisions, and non-reliance clauses to the maximum extent enforceable by law.
* **Analysis & Action:** It is a non-negotiable buyer protection that liability for fraud or deliberate concealment cannot be contractually capped or limited. Insert explicit carve-outs across all limitation clauses.

#### D. Disclosure Scope & Buyer Knowledge (Schedule 7 & Clause 8.3)
* **Deemed General Disclosure (Schedule 7):** The Seller attempts general disclosure of the entire electronic data room (DD-002 to DD-012) and all public registers.
  * *Playbook Position:* Reject data-room-wide, public-register, or prudent-search deemed disclosures. Disclosures must be specific and fairly disclosed against specific warranties.
* **Buyer Knowledge Bar (Clause 8.3):** The Seller excludes claims for matters of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge (including constructive knowledge from the data room or public records).
  * *Playbook Position:* Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions and constructive knowledge bars. Any seller knowledge qualifier must be limited to named Seller individuals after reasonable inquiry, and must *never* qualify Title, Capacity, Fraud, or Specific Indemnities.

#### E. Key Material Contracts & Debt Obligations
* **Bluefen Consent (Clauses 3 / 6.3 & Disclosure 2):** Bluefen represents ~30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6M). The Seller proposes a "reasonable endeavours" obligation and treats consent as satisfied upon simple delivery of written consent, ignoring the operational conditions in clause 11.3.
  * *Playbook Position:* Require effective, unconditional consent **and** evidence that associated conditions (cl 11.3) are satisfied *prior* to Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient.
* **Riverlark Bank Facility (Clauses 2 / 7 & Disclosure 3):** AUD 3.2M outstanding facility. Seller proposes a post-completion security release.
  * *Playbook Position:* Transaction is cash-free/debt-free. Require direct payout from Completion funds flow and effective security releases delivered at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking from the lender plus express written approval from Amelia Frost.
* **Employee Completion Bonuses (Disclosure 5):** AUD 420,000 in conditional bonuses (DD-005). Seller claims this is a matter for the Seller and omits it from the draft Completion funds flow.
  * *Playbook Position:* Must be specifically itemized in the funds flow or funded directly by the Seller, explicitly accounting for associated payroll tax, superannuation, and on-costs. It cannot be silently left as a post-closing liability of the Target.

#### F. Specific Indemnities, Privacy Incident & Title Proof
* **Ironquay IP Indemnity (Clause 11.1 & Disclosure 4):** Seller limits the indemnity to the specific SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000 open).
  * *Playbook Position:* Broaden the IP indemnity to cover all IP ownership risks and third-party infringement claims arising from Ironquay development, preserving the SOW3 cure. Note that the AUD 180,000 figure is not independently verified by bank records.
* **Export / Privacy Incident (DD-006 & Disclosure 6):** An unintended email export containing ~1,240 records. Seller dismisses it as non-material.
  * *Playbook Position:* Require contractual undertakings/warranties to preserve system logs, complete the formal investigation, provide regular updates, and maintain an indemnity for potential regulatory notification or remediation costs. Concurrently, maintain our DD position assuming no confirmed breach or quantified loss figure.
* **Sandbar Renewals (DD-008, DD-011 & Disclosure 8):** Three supplier renewals totalling AUD 330,000.
  * *Playbook Position:* Assess operational necessity, terminability, and accrual. Do not automatically classify as Debt or force a price deduction without contract review, but ensure they are in the ordinary course.
* **Title Verification (Disclosure 10):** Seller relies solely on DD-012 (Company share register) as proof of share title.
  * *Playbook Position:* Internal share registers are not independent proof. Require independent legal title and encumbr
